answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked before it can influence a market, then forfeited if independent audits find duplicate identities or fabricated work. A reputation-weighted reward pool pays only after delayed peer validation, so one operator cannot cheaply multiply votes to claim immediate rewards. The bond can be denominated in pigment, basalt, or cedar, but the real cost is capital tied up across every suspected identity, plus audit exposure and lost reputation when a Sybil cluster is caught.
